config.disableFullAccessColor: Show full-access tasks without the red warning colour. Off (default): their Queue row is red, as before. On: the row keeps its `!!` badge and tooltip in the normal colour, and the Task view shows a small **⚠ full access** note instead of the red **FULL ACCESS** badge.
config.fullAccessIdleConfirm: Before you send a reply, an option or a quick prompt to a **full-access** task, or add a task that gets full access from the confirmed default for **+**, ask first when you have not added a task or a reply to that queue for this long. `never` = never ask. The picker's own FULL ACCESS question is not repeated, and an automatic answer (Auto-pick best) never asks.
config.fullAccessIdleConfirm.4h: Ask when the queue was not used for 4 hours.
config.fullAccessIdleConfirm.1d: Ask when the queue was not used for 1 day.
config.fullAccessIdleConfirm.7d: Ask when the queue was not used for 7 days.
config.autoRunInFullAccess: **Off** by default. When on, a **full**-access task that stops with a command for you to run (its last message has a shell code block, or one with no language) gets it run by itself by its open Task view, once per question, in a new, visible terminal in the task's folder, and the chat says so. The first time for each task a box shows the exact command first: **Run** or **Run and don't ask again for this task**; closing the box runs nothing. Several lines always ask, with all their lines; several PowerShell lines are copied for you to paste and check instead (never `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`). Other profiles never run anything by themselves: the block is highlighted with a **Run silently** button. You still reply so the task continues.
config.autoContinueAfterLimit: Continue automatically after a usage limit resets. Off (default): when Claude hits the usage limit, the queue is put on hold and a notification asks whether to continue after the reset (**Continue after reset**, **Always** turns this on, **Not now** keeps the hold; **Resume Queue (Release Hold)** in the Queue view continues it later). On: the runner waits for the reset and resumes the same task by itself. User settings only.
config.defaultUltracode: Ultracode for every new task: each attempt passes `--settings {"ultracode":true}` to Claude Code (standing workflow orchestration at any effort). It runs many agents, so it uses much more of your usage, and it needs a model that supports ultracode. Only with the `full` profile and subagents (the Workflow tool is offered only there); any other task gets it off. Off: nothing is passed. The **+ Add new task** panel (next to Effort) and **Defaults for +** set it; **Provider, Model, Effort…** changes one task.
config.defaultAutorun: Autorun for every new task: when the task asks a question with options, Sleeping Clanker answers it with the best (recommended) option itself, also while its Task view is closed, and starts the queue's runner for the answer (never on a held queue). The Task view shows no option buttons for it, only `Autorun picked: …`. It never changes the permission profile; a permission denial still waits for you, and after 20 automatic answers in a row the next question waits too, as does a question that came back. It needs a VS Code window open on the task's project: with the core alone (`run` from a terminal) the question waits. Set it in the **+ Add new task** panel's Other settings or **Defaults for +**; ⚙ Chat settings in a Task view switches one task.
config.limitForecastWarning: Before you queue a task or send a reply, warn when the usage-limit forecast says the limit will likely be hit before a typical task finishes (or a limit window is at 95% or more), and offer Send anyway, Queue for after the reset or Cancel. The forecast comes from the usage data in your own task runs; nothing is sent anywhere.
cmd.sendForFix: Send Errors to Claude for a Fix…
config.language.enum.auto: Follow VS Code's display language when it is English, Russian or Finnish; otherwise English.
config.language.description: The language of the extension's own UI: the Queue view, the status bar, the hovers, the New Task panel and the Task view (chat). The gear button in the Queue view (**Global settings → Language**) and the New Task panel (**Other settings → Language**) change it at once. Menu command names and this Settings page follow VS Code's display language (`Configure Display Language`): Russian has an official VS Code language pack; Finnish has none, so with Finnish they stay in VS Code's language.

This project's queue is empty.
[Add…](command:claudAutopilot.add)
[Start Runner](command:claudAutopilot.startRunner)
[Show All Projects](command:claudAutopilot.showAllProjects)
[Defaults for +…](command:claudAutopilot.addDefaults)
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces: Sleeping Clanker runs Claude Code with file-edit permissions inside workspace folders.
config.dataDir: Base folder for the queues and logs; each project gets its own `projects\<name>-<hash>` folder inside it. Empty = the core default (`%CLAUDE_AUTOPILOT_HOME%`, else `%LOCALAPPDATA%\claud_autopilot`).
config.defaultProfile: Permission profile listed first when adding a task — and, with claudAutopilot.askProfile off, the one every new task gets without asking. Never full: FULL ACCESS is chosen per task, with a confirmation. User settings only (a workspace cannot set it).
config.defaultProfile.safe: Recommended. Read/Edit/Write/Glob/Grep, edits only inside the task folder; no shell, no web.
config.defaultProfile.edits: Auto-approve edits; Bash, PowerShell, WebFetch and WebSearch stay disallowed.
config.defaultProfile.plan: Read-only plan mode: Read/Glob/Grep only; makes a plan, changes nothing.
config.defaultProfile.shell-read: Like safe, plus a fixed list of read-only commands (exact git status/log/diff forms, Get-ChildItem/ls, Get-Content/cat, Select-String, findstr); every other command is denied. No deleting, no installs, no ssh, no web.
config.defaultProfile.shell-dev: Like shell-read, plus the commands on this project's allow-list (Edit Allowed Commands…; kept in the autopilot data folder, never the repo). This is not a sandbox: the commands you allow run with your rights (a test runner, interpreter or build tool runs any code the task writes, and that code can push, delete, install and reach the web); only a fixed list of risky programs is refused. An empty list = shell-read.
config.defaultKind: What the **+** button adds without showing the Add menu. The `Defaults for +` rows at the bottom of the Queue view write this.
config.defaultKind.ask: Show the Add menu, as in 0.4.3 and earlier.
config.defaultKind.task: Add a one-shot task: + asks only for the prompt.
config.defaultKind.goal: Set a goal Claude keeps pursuing: + asks only for the goal.
config.defaultKind.plan: A task that only plans and changes nothing.
config.defaultKind.files: Attach files or folders first, then ask task or goal.
config.askProfile: Ask the permission profile for every new task. Off: every new task gets `#claudAutopilot.defaultProfile#` without asking (plan-mode tasks stay `plan`). User settings only (a workspace cannot set it).
config.defaultLane: The queue a new task goes to without asking, when the project has two or more queues. Empty = ask (last used first). A queue that no longer exists is ignored, and the picker appears again.
config.askGoalCaps: Ask the round and time cap for every new goal. Off: a new goal gets `#claudAutopilot.goalMaxRounds#` and `#claudAutopilot.goalMaxHours#` without asking.
config.showAddPanel: Show the `New Task` panel under the Queue view. Its title-bar X turns this off; `Sleeping Clanker: Show the New Task panel` (Queue view `...` menu or Command Palette) turns it back on.
config.showAddDefaults: Show the `Defaults for +` rows at the bottom of the Queue view. Off: change them from the Command Palette (`Sleeping Clanker: Defaults for +…`).
config.groupByStatus: Sort each queue in the Queue view into **Questions** (on top), **Running**, **Not done yet**, **Errors**, **Not completed** and **Completed** (newest first). Click a group's arrow to hide or show it. A main task and its subtasks stay together. Off: one flat list, as in 0.4.6.
config.autoPickBestOption: In an open Task view (chat), answer a blocked task's question automatically with its best option — the one Claude marked **recommended**, otherwise its first option. Off by default: every question waits for you. An automatic answer never widens the task's permission profile (a manual click on a shell option still may), it is sent once per question, and at most 5 times in a row for one task before the chat waits for you again. Each chat has its own `Auto-pick best` box next to the reply box; this setting is what a newly opened chat starts with.
config.runCodeSilently: A chat code block's **Run in terminal** runs it in a hidden terminal: no terminal window opens (a note offers **Show terminal**). The command is still shown for you to confirm first. A blocked task's command that must run for it to continue always gets its own highlighted **Run silently** button.
config.changesQuestion: The reply the Task view's **What did you change?** button sends to a finished, failed or cancelled task. Claude is asked for a short final message (1-3 lines), and this button asks for the details on demand. Example: `List the changed files with their paths and the setting or option each change adds.` Empty = no button.
config.quickPrompts: Quick prompts: one button each above the Task view's reply box, shown whenever the task can take a reply (blocked, done, failed, cancelled or paused, with a session). A click sends that text as your reply, with the profile in the dropdown; **Shift+click** puts it in the reply box so you can edit it first. Up to 8, each up to 2000 characters. Example: `Write a short summary for the changelog.` Empty list = no buttons.
config.fixProject: The Sleeping Clanker source folder that **Send Errors to Claude for a Fix…** queues its fix task in. Empty = pick the folder the first time (it is saved here).
config.refreshSeconds: Refresh interval while the Queue view is visible or a runner is alive (otherwise 30 s).
config.maxTurns: 0 = use the core default (100 per task, 40 per goal round). A value above 0 is passed to `run --max-turns` (the per-task turn cap).
config.autoStartRunner: Start runners automatically: when VS Code starts (the main queue plus every other queue of the project with pending or waiting tasks), and after you queue a task or send a reply to a queue whose runner is not running. On by default; turn it off here to start runners yourself. The "Always start automatically" button on the queued message turns it back on. User settings only: a workspace cannot change it.
config.model: Claude model for queued tasks. Empty = the runner's default: `claude-opus-5-5` with effort `high` (set by the core, or by the environment variables `CLAUDE_AUTOPILOT_MODEL` / `CLAUDE_AUTOPILOT_EFFORT` that VS Code was started with). A value here (for example `sonnet`) overrides the model only and is passed as `--claude-arg=--model=<value>`. There is no effort setting: effort stays `high` unless `CLAUDE_AUTOPILOT_EFFORT` is set. A task's own model (`#claudAutopilot.askModel#`, or **Change Model…** on a task) wins over this one.
config.askModel: Ask the model for every new task (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, Fable or any model id). Off: every new task uses the runner's model (`#claudAutopilot.model#`). Either way, **Change Model…** on a task that is not running sets its model for the next attempt.
config.defaultProvider: The model provider of every new task (`claude`, `claude-api`, `deepseek`, `kimi`, `glm`, `qwen`, `codex`, `bedrock`, `custom`; `providers` lists them and which keys are set). Empty = the runner's provider (normally Claude on the subscription). The **+ Add new task** panel under the queue sets it. A provider with an API key only runs with the `safe`, `edits` or `plan` profile.
config.defaultModel: The model id of every new task. Empty = the provider's default (on the runner's provider: `#claudAutopilot.model#`). The **+ Add new task** panel sets it; when it is set, `#claudAutopilot.askModel#` does not ask.
config.defaultEffort: The effort (`--effort`) of every new task. Empty = the runner's. Left out for a provider that takes none (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Qwen, Codex, custom). The **+ Add new task** panel sets it.
config.splitTasks: Split a new task's prompt that lists several tasks into one queued task per item, in the same queue (they run one after another). A list is 2+ lines starting with `1.`/`1)` or `-`/`*` (a bullet list under other text only when that text says "tasks"), or `1. … 2. …` on one line; each item needs 2+ words. The text around the list is given to every part. Applies to New Task, Plan and Task with files, not to goals, selections or prompt files. Off: the prompt is always one task.
config.tasksAtOnce: Tasks at once: how many tasks of one queue run at the same time (1-5). Each runs in its own private copy of the project and is merged back when it finishes; a merge conflict asks you. 1 (default): one after another, as before. A change applies to a running runner of this window at its next pick.
config.newTaskStart: With **Tasks at once** above 1: when a newly added task may start.
config.newTaskStart.whenFree: As soon as a slot is free, beside the tasks already running (default).
config.newTaskStart.afterPrevious: Only after the task added before it has finished and its changes are merged.
config.defaultMaxAgents: How many helper agents (subagents) a **new** task may start (`add --max-agents`). Each task keeps its own limit: the dropdown at the bottom of its Task view, or `edit <id> --max-agents`. A subagent gets the task's own permissions, nothing more; the count is asked for in the system prompt, and the run log says so if a task went over it.
config.defaultMaxAgents.default: The permission profile decides: only `full` may start subagents (as before).
config.defaultMaxAgents.none: No subagents: the Agent tool is denied.
config.defaultMaxAgents.unlimited: As many subagents as the task needs.
config.maxParallelRunners: How many queues this window may run at the same time. `0` = no limit (as before). A queue asked to start while the limit is reached waits, and starts by itself when a runner finishes. Only runners this window started are counted and held back.
config.goalMaxRounds: Default round cap for a new goal (add --goal --max-rounds). -1 = unlimited: the goal runs until it is stopped (or its hour cap).
config.taskView: What a double-click on a task (and Open Task View) opens. Open Raw Log always opens the text log.
config.taskView.chat: The Task view: a chat-style panel with rendered answers, compact tool rows and a reply box.
config.taskView.text: The raw text log (a read-only document), as before 0.4.0.
config.logPolling: Log every background refresh call (status, lanes, projects, where...) in the Sleeping Clanker output channel. Off: a refresh call is logged only when it fails or is slow (over 5 s). For debugging.
config.goalMaxHours: Default time cap in hours for a new goal (add --goal --max-hours).
